source_review.notes: Reviewed ten sources covering architecture quality scenarios, ISO quality models and architecture descriptions, QAW, accessibility, distributed data, performance analysis, and indicator validity. Crossref metadata confirmed the three cited report/article DOI identities; official W3C WCAG 2.2 content confirmed the current 12 December 2024 Recommendation date and its explicit limit that not every user need is addressed; official IEEE 42010 and publisher architecture-book pages returned successfully. The official ISO 25010 catalog endpoint identified the cited standard but denied automated page retrieval, so its 2023 identity was checked without claiming page-content verification. No mutable vendor behavior is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed the six-part scenario tuple, scoped measure tuple, violation proportion, latency quantile, measurement boundaries, workload context, guardrail and oracle sets, and scenario-suite coverage notation.
Confirmed populations, units, proportions, quantiles, time boundaries, sets, and symbols are defined before use and enclosed in supported math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Quantile interpretation is explicitly conditioned on convention, ties, eligible population, timeouts, and errors.

evidence: Recomputed one percent of 1,000,000 eligible observations as 10,000 observations.
Checked all latency, rate, duration, freshness, success, error, revocation, and recovery thresholds for dimensional consistency within their scenarios.
Confirmed scenario thresholds are declared design inputs rather than fabricated observed measurements.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No percentile example is presented as a maximum or as evidence about an unobserved deployed system.

evidence: Verified r=k/N is dimensionless when k is the violating subset of N eligible observations.
Verified 1-q is the fraction that may lie beyond a q-quantile boundary under the stated population and quantile caveats.
Verified the scenario and measure tuples preserve distinct stimulus source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, population, statistic, threshold, window, and exclusions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The tuple is a completeness model for analysis, not a theorem that six filled fields guarantee a valid requirement.

evidence: Reviewed nominal, peak, skewed, cold, degraded, disconnected, recovery, mixed-version, migration, retirement, misuse, compromised, and second-fault conditions.
Reviewed survivor bias, timeouts excluded from latency, stale cache as availability, missing telemetry as zero, aggregation hiding cohorts, and target-driven metric gaming.
Reviewed credential revocation, accessibility under incident load, privacy deletion and restore, fraud, intermittent field use, perishable goods, and physical or human consequences.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Scenario selection explicitly preserves severe minority and mandatory safety, security, privacy, accessibility, and legal concerns.

evidence: Traced every worked scenario through source, stimulus, environment, artifact, response, and measure or used it to diagnose a missing component.
Confirmed mechanisms remain distinct from responses and component telemetry remains distinct from end-to-end outcome oracles.
Confirmed error, timeout, stale, missing, duplicate, unauthorized, degraded, and unknown outcomes cannot silently count as useful success.
invariant_checking.notes: Portfolio invariants include evidence scope, expiry, anti-gaming guardrails, stakeholder legitimacy, and explicit omissions.

evidence: Reviewed the p99 counterexample and confirmed a quantile threshold cannot imply a maximum or describe the magnitude of the remaining tail.
Reviewed the survivor-bias argument and confirmed conditioning on successful endpoint arrivals removes precisely the missing and timed-out observations at issue.
Reviewed the response-versus-mechanism counterexamples for queues, caches, failover, and autoscaling.
proof_review.notes: The chapter presents scoped measurement arguments and proof obligations, not a formal proof of system quality.

evidence: Audited uses of available, current, complete, reliable, secure, correct, conformance, guarantee, prove, valid, and exhaustive for explicit scope and limitations.
Verified calculations, benchmarks, fault exercises, usability studies, conformance checks, and qualitative judgments retain distinct evidence meanings.
Verified quality-model categories and stakeholder votes are not represented as priorities or acceptance authority by themselves.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Passing scenarios are never generalized into universal quality claims.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter specifies measurement and evidence designs but reports no executed benchmark, accessibility study, fault campaign, security assessment, disaster-relief field trial, or production observation.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed all six scenario components, scoped measures, attribute-specific forms, lifecycle, scenario families, stakeholder elicitation, prioritization, architecture tracing, oracles, metric gaming, evidence strength, quality conflicts, and portfolio review for coherence and appropriate ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed search latency, survivor bias, useful availability, credential revocation, mixed-version tax change, accessible incident operation, percentile tails, regional recovery, energy optimization, and hospital isolation. Verified each exposes implementable architectural decisions and measurable failure conditions. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth measurement and governance reasoning, eighteen distinct misconceptions, ten nonduplicative worked examples with explicit conclusions, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar international disaster-relief transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checking, arithmetic, and scenario analysis do not constitute an executed benchmark, reliability campaign, accessibility study, security or privacy assessment, physical validation, humanitarian field evaluation, regulatory determination, or quality guarantee.
